turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. You asked for this meeting, so start with why my son's essay got a zero before anyone called me.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what you have that made you enter it.
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
I'm not reading times off a screen until you answer my question. Procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first, so did you speak with Owen before you entered that zero?
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.

You still haven't told me whether you spoke to Owen before you entered the zero. You gave a student a mark first and now you're asking him to prove himself afterward. The zero comes off today, and I'm writing that down.
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Which line, Hale? Read me exactly what the essay says, and I'll search the act myself. A misquote is a mistake students make, so I'm writing down what you read me before I decide what it proves.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.

A forty-minute in-class piece and a take-home essay with the play open beside it are different things, Hale. You still haven't read me the line from Act 3, Scene 2, and I'm writing down that you skipped it. Put the September 24 page and that line in front of me where I can read them.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4. In writing tonight, copying the principal, with nothing on his record. I haven't agreed to a rewrite, because you still haven't put the line or the September 24 page in front of me. Until I've read them, the zero comes out of the gradebook today.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to put a supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 in writing tonight, private, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the exact line you say is not in Act 3, Scene 2 and the September 24 page, and the zero out of the gradebook today. You said tonight, so I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Fallback; she has not agreed to the rewrite, and she still wants the zero out of the gradebook today plus the line from Act 3 and the September 24 page in front of her, so the fair outcome (a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, procedure 4.4) is on the table but not accepted, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You cited 4.4 correctly and committed to it in writing, because that met her fallback demand of keeping this quiet and off his record.
What cost ground: You never read her the line you said was not in the play when she asked for it, because it left your strongest claim as something she could not check.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with the essay created late the night before it was due, came closest to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open with the line from the play and the September 24 page in your hands, and answer her question about speaking to Owen first, before you show anything from that late night.
